Answer: B
Reason: The initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a) displays a bilateral reticulonodular pattern with superimposed ground-glass opacities and air-space consolidation, consistent with acute lupus pneumonitis. The control X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates rapid resolution of the parenchymal consolidation but shows persistence of bilateral pleural effusions (blunted costophrenic angles), which is a common chronic manifestation of SLE.
